claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I have a few follow-up questions:

Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? (This is important because Child Benefit eligibility can continue up to age 20 if the child stays in qualifying education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that Alex is in full-time education doing his A-levels.

Now I have a couple more questions to assess your eligibility:

1. **Are you responsible for Alex?** This usually means he lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now, could you tell me a bit about your own situation:

**Are you living in the UK?** (This includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question:

**What is your immigration or nationality status?** For example, are you a British or Irish citizen, or do you have settled status or another immigration status that allows you to claim benefits in the UK?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me and the eligibility rules, I now have enough information to make a determination about your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- Alex is 16 years old
- He is in full-time approved education (A-levels at college)
- He lives with you in Manchester, UK
- You are a British citizen
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **You live in the UK** – You're based in Manchester  
✅ **You're a British citizen** – You have the right to claim benefits  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** – He lives with you  
✅ **Alex qualifies** – Although he's 16, he's in full-time approved education (A-levels), which means Child Benefit can continue until he finishes this education or turns 20, whichever comes first  
✅ **No competing claims** – No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Just remember to notify the Child Benefit Office if Alex's education or training situation changes in the future.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
